subject: Information Theory
title: Entropy in Genetics
description: A tiny lesson with a big payoff: Entropy in Genetics.

hook.text: DNA uses four letters: A, T, C, G. If equally distributed, each position carries 2 bits of entropy.

buildup.text: But real genomes aren't uniform. Some regions are highly conserved—low entropy—while others vary widely.

discovery.text: Conserved regions like ribosomal RNA genes have low entropy: evolution keeps them nearly identical across species.

twist.text: High-entropy regions evolve faster. They're where adaptation happens—mutations tolerated and sometimes rewarded.

climax.text: Entropy maps of genomes reveal which regions matter most and which are free to drift.

punchline.text: Low entropy in DNA means evolution says don't touch.

quiz.question: What does low entropy in a DNA region indicate?
options: The region is highly conserved by evolution
